articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.
articles.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again

articles.author: Juliana Kim
articles.description: The proposed rule is a major step forward in addressing a form of fraud that has robbed SNAP recipients of millions.
articles.title: Trump administration pushes for food assistance card upgrade to fight fraud

articles.author: Nate Perez
articles.description: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.
articles.title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey

articles.author: Maureen Corrigan
articles.description: Elizabeth McCracken's connected short stories chronicle a family's encounters with their eldest son's girlfriend and eventual wife. This slim collection is so engaging, you may want to read it twice.
articles.title: These 'Seven Stories About Tammy' add up to one brilliant piece of writing

articles.author: John Ruwitch
articles.description: The AI company, which makes the popular Claude chatbot, has filed for an initial public offering that could be one of the biggest ever.
articles.title: AI giant Anthropic files for an IPO that could break records

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Andre McKechnie, 55, is serving a life sentence for murder. He took his battle for the salty, sticky, black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the court last year. He argued being refused Vegemite breached the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act.
articles.title: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: This closed-door gathering that started Monday comes about a year before Xi is expected to secure a fourth term and personnel changes to key leadership bodies.
articles.title: What to know about China's plenum as Xi seeks stronger party discipline

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: President Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States.
articles.title: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan

articles.author: Jessica Meszaros
articles.description: Hurricane forecasters are increasingly using artificial intelligence to make predictions.
articles.title: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts

articles.author: Kirk Siegler
articles.description: President Trump is planning to open up some of the nation's last pristine forests to road building and timber companies. But those who work in the woods say it won't do enough to revive the industry.
articles.title: Loggers say Roadless Rule repeal won't solve their biggest challenges

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Political debate should be ‘robust but respectful’, Anne Ruston says
A day after MPs addressed the House of Representatives paying tribute to the independent Helen Haines, who was injured after an alleged attack in her electorate, the Liberal senator Anne Ruston maintains that respect is necessary in political debate.
What we do here sets the tone for what the rest of the nation thinks is acceptable.
There is a huge responsibility on politicians, not to shy away from robust debate. I don’t want anyone to think that we shouldn’t be having strong debate.
It’s simply out of control in an online world and we’ve got to make the platforms accountable.
Facebook is the worst in terms of the platforms, Instagram and TikTok less so, but still bad.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian politics live: Coalition tells Albanese to ‘stop the spin’ on $6m golf grant; Labor promises ‘swift response’ on MP safety

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
US military says the restrictions on the electric vehicles at Kadena airbase also apply to delivery drivers and taxis
One of America’s biggest overseas military bases has banned vehicles made by the Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD over security concerns, the US military in Japan said on Tuesday.
The ban, which went into effect this week at Kadena airbase on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa, has fueled speculation that similar measures could be taken at other US military facilities as part of Washington’s crackdown on Chinese technology it suspects of being used to collect sensitive information.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US bans vehicles from China’s BYD at Japan military base, calling them ‘unacceptable’ risk

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
NSW police officer accused of murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies tells court he wanted to do ‘right thing’ by their families

Follow our Australian politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has accused a friend of encouraging him to dispose of the bodies of two men “straight away”, despite him wanting to report the deaths to police, according to his first statement to his double murder trial.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon tells jury he wanted to report deaths but friend encouraged him to dispose of bodies

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

What are the US midterm elections and why do they matter?


Sign up for Breaking News US email

In a post to social media on Monday, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was facing dwindling stocks of Patriot interceptor missiles after Pete Hegseth, Trump’s defense secretary, had delayed authorizing new supplies.
“We have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr. Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS,” Zelenskyy wrote. “I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again. Conversations with other countries are also ongoing.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in Mississippi amid outcry over racist, Islamophobic attacks – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
This is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to challenge states with competitive midterm races that could determine control of Congress
The Trump administration on Monday asked Washington state to set aside any ballots received from more than 400 people it alleges are registered to vote without US citizenship, less than two weeks after making a similar demand in California.
The announcement is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to sow doubts about the election or its outcome in states with races that will help determine control of the US Senate and House.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration asks Washington to set aside hundreds of ballots from suspected noncitizen voters

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
Newsom accuses Trump of ‘assault on democracy’ as DoJ claims 20,000 registered voters in state are non-citizens
A US federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration’s move to block California from counting the ballots of 20,000 registered voters that the justice department claims are non-citizens.
The court on Monday ruled 2-1 against Donald ⁠Trump’s ​justice department in the dispute, denying the administration’s demand that election officials segregate the thousands of ballots until people on the list could verify their citizenship. The justice department had given the California secretary of state 48-hours to carry out the order, which state election officials refused – leading to the lawsuit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Court blocks bid by Trump DoJ to stop California from counting mail-in ballots

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Tasks from determining asylum seekers’ ages to border surveillance now involve AI, says Open Rights Group 
AI has been embedded across the Home Office in near-total secrecy, reinforcing the so-called hostile environment for immigration, according to research.
Tasks from the detection of potential sham marriages to determining the age of asylum seekers and checking through the contents of phones of new arrivals now involve use of the technology, according to a report by Open Rights Group (ORG).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Digital hostile environment’: AI secretly being embedded across Home Office, report claims

articles.author: Phillip Inman Senior economics writer
articles.description:
British Retail Consortium says ‘dam is starting to break on the huge wave of costs’ being kept from consumers
Shop price inflation has risen to the highest level in two and a half years, according to the British Retail Consortium, which warned that “the dam is starting to break” when it comes to retailers trying to limit price rises for customers.
The lobby group said shop price inflation was 2.1% year on year in October, a sharp rise compared with 1.4% in September, and an indication that retailers were beginning to pass on the rising costs of energy and food ingredients since the Middle East conflict broke out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK shop price inflation ‘highest since 2024’ as retailers struggle to limit price rises

articles.author: Tom Phillips, Michael Hubbard and Guardian moderators
articles.description:
Having lost the first round of Brazil’s presidential election to far right rival Flávio Bolsonaro, incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva spectacularly triumphed in the second. What comes next for Brazil? The Guardian’s Tom Phillips will be answering your questions from 15:00 GMT today.
Ask a question: log in or sign up here to comment, or email conversations@theguardian.com
After losing the first round of Brazil’s presidential election to far right rival Flávio Bolsonaro, incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, better known simply as Lula, pulled off the most stunning political fightback in modern Brazilian history by winning the second, in so doing securing a fourth presidential term. It will see him become the country’s longest-serving leader.
The result – 51.79% to Lula, 48.21% to Bolsonaro – was delivered after a supreme court judge had extended polling time by two hours, and after Lula’s camp accused their opponents of sabotaging public transport in an attempt to keep their voters from the polls. It was the first time in Brazilian electoral history that a first-round verdict had been overturned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reader Q&A: After Lula’s sensational victory in Brazil’s presidential election, post your questions for the Guardian’s Latin America correspondent

articles.author: Barry Yeoman
articles.description:
Suit that cites 2025 Guardian investigation alleges ‘pattern of inaccurate pricing’ that ‘affects millions of purchases’
The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states have sued Dollar General, the nation’s largest dollar-store chain, for persistently overcharging customers at its more than 20,000 stores across the United States.
The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Nashville, cites a Guardian investigation published last December.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, accusing bargain chain of overcharging customers

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Brasília
articles.description:
Far-right senator banned from leaving country as supreme court judge’s ruling makes reference to money-laundering case
The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro was banned from leaving Brazil and ordered to surrender his passports just hours after his dramatic loss in the presidential election to the leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
The ruling was issued by supreme court justice Alexandre de Moraes, the same justice who oversaw the trial of the senator’s father, the former president Jair Bolsonaro, for attempting a coup.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil: defeated Flávio Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports

articles.author: Patrick Commins
articles.description:
Australia’s public debt may be well below that of France but there are lessons to be taken from its economic woes

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The explosion of discontent that led to major protests and violence in France and across Europe is a “warning signal” that Australia could follow the same path without an “honest conversation” about the budget, economists say.
Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday to protest against school underfunding, as complaints of insufficient teacher numbers and dilapidated infrastructure mingled with broader discontent about cost-of-living pressures.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The chaos in France is a ‘warning signal’ for Australia’s public spending and rising costs

articles.author: Lucy Campbell
articles.description:
Last Ditch bar announced it would ‘soft close’ after it went viral following a story on its attempt to relax Covid rules
A Massachusetts lesbian bar that went viral for loosening its Covid mask policy last month announced plans to “soft close” on Monday as it seeks new ownership.
The Last Ditch bar, in the small city of Greenfield, said in an Instagram post that it was searching for co-owners, new owners or a full sale, and that it would “soft close effective immediately”, with “only booked events” continuing while it closes this winter. It had opened just last year as a bar for “dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers, and their friends”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Massachusetts lesbian bar makes frantic effort to find new owners after relaxing masking policy

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Controversial mechanism that hit unpaid carers with huge penalties to be scrapped following Guardian investigation
The controversial rule that led to unpaid carers being punished with penalties amounting to thousands of pounds is to be abolished, the Guardian can reveal.
The chancellor, John Healey, is to announce a new digital taper system for carer’s allowance in Wednesday’s budget, effectively ending what is regarded as one of the UK benefit system’s most feared and unfair administrative practices.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Carers allowed to earn over the weekly limit without losing out as ‘cliff-edge’ abolished in the budget

articles.author: Associated Press in Amman
articles.description:
Jordanian air force says it carried out strikes against ‘terrorist groups’ tied to killing of nine in Karak
Jordan has carried out airstrikes against armed groups in Syria in retaliation for Friday’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Jordanian city of Karak that killed nine people, the Jordanian air force has said in a statement.
It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. It did not specify who the groups were or the precise location of the strikes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jordan attacks militants in Syria in retaliation for last week’s church attack

articles.author: Sinéad Campbell
articles.description:
Group was on visit to meet Palestinian children, farmers and civil leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces
An international delegation including British politicians has been barred from entering the West Bank on a trip to meet Palestinian children, farmers and society leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces during olive harvest season.
The delegation of 23 people, including four elected representatives, was drawn from countries including France, Spain, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Greece, Holland, Ireland and the US. It included the Labour MP Clive Lewis, the Scottish National party MP Lara Bird, the Scottish Greens MSP Kate Nevens and the former Labour MP Sam Tarry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British politicians among international delegates barred from entering West Bank

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Fraser coast mayor described James Hansen as ‘always ready to help others, contribute to the community and advocate strongly’

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

James Hansen, a former Queensland councillor, has been identified as the man who died in flooding on the state’s Fraser Coast.
Hansen, 57, was a dairy farmer and fourth-generation resident of the area. He served as a councillor for the Fraser Coast regional council between 2012 and 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man found dead in Queensland floods named as former councillor and One Nation candidate

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
Activists say struggle must go on until their ‘maximum’ demands are met over teacher shortages and building repairs
French children should continue to barricade their schools and take part in street protests, a student union said on Monday after the government announced a package of education measures to try to stem the crisis.
“Today we’re at the negotiating table, we’re able to negotiate with the government,” Pierre Sourzat of Les Lycéens told France Info television. “We’re in a power struggle and we still need to call for continued mobilisation to meet a maximum of our demands.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protest leaders urge French pupils to keep barricading their schools

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Brand, charged with rape and sexual assault, was ‘sleeping with people day and night’, former assistant alleges 
Russell Brand had an “insane sexual appetite” and his bad behaviour was “normalised and dismissed” by those around him, his former personal assistant has told a court.
Helen Berger alleged she had seen Brand treat women badly and that she once had to stop his mother and girlfriend walking in on him having sex with someone in his dressing room.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand had ‘insane sexual appetite’ and his bad behaviour was normalised, trial told

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison and Julian Borger in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Israeli prime minister increases alarmist rhetoric as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in polls
Benjamin Netanyahu has resorted to increasingly alarmist rhetoric and reportedly put pressure on Israel’s military to take action against Iran as his far-right coalition narrowly trails in the polls ahead of Tuesday’s close-run elections.
The Israeli prime minister posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear mushroom cloud destroying Tel Aviv, telling Israeli voters to choose him or risk nuclear annihilation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Netanyahu reportedly pressured military to attack Iran in run-up to election

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Company says small number of devices affected by display glitch after posts appear on Reddit and social media
Owners of the new foldable iPhone are reporting cracks in the device’s screen, as Apple confirmed an issue with a “small number” of units.
Reports of cracks have emerged on Reddit and social media platforms since the handset went on general sale globally on Friday. Experts said there had been too few examples to determine whether there was a more serious problem with Apple’s first foldable device, which retails from $1,999 (£1,499).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: iPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handset

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Badr Albusaidi calls for security pact involving Gulf states, Iraq and Iran with US no longer primary provider of security 
The Middle East’s ability to solve its problems has been held back by America’s 50-year insistence that the Gulf states should view Iran as a security threat, Oman’s foreign minister said on Monday in a significant speech designed to break the deadlock over the region’s future.
Badr Albusaidi called for a non-aggression security pact involving all six Gulf states as well as Iran and Iraq. The US would in future no longer be the primary provider of security, he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Middle East peace held back by US insistence that Iran is a threat, Oman’s foreign minister says

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
More strong winds forecast after Austen and Boelo kill two people and bring travel disruption and flooding

Tell us: have you been affected by Storm Boelo and Storm Austen

A major clean-up operation was under way on Monday after weekend storms caused havoc, with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come.
Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, struck parts of the UK, and there was widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Major clean-up under way after two storms cause havoc in Britain

articles.author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
articles.description:
Clarification comes after PM fuelled speculation about EU-UK relationship in series of interviews at weekend
Downing Street has been forced to clarify Andy Burnham’s stance on whether the UK would return to having freedom of movement with the EU after the prime minister said an “honest discussion” was needed on the issue.
Burnham fuelled speculation about a return to freedom of movement in an interview at the weekend, prompting questions about how close the UK could become to Brussels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 clarifies Andy Burnham’s stance on freedom of movement

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Brasília and Tom Phillips in São Paulo
articles.description:
A viral WhatsApp channel and student-led protests played a key role in the veteran Brazilian leftist’s election victory
After the first round of the Brazilian presidential election three weeks ago, the leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reportedly told allies he could not understand how he finished second after a government he considered the best of his three terms.
A mood of dismay swept Brazil’s left, and because 9 million voters for the other candidates, all of them on the right, were expected to mostly transfer to senator Flávio Bolsonaro, analysts widely saw the far-right senator’s victory as certain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How the streets and social media drove Lula to a historic comeback in Brazil

articles.author: Presented by Michael Safi with Tom Phillips; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Bryony Moore
articles.description:
Brazil’s Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a historic fourth term as president, defeating the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a dramatic comeback.
Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%. His win bucks a regional trend, after the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro had spearheaded a radical populist movement.
But with Flávio Bolsonaro refusing to concede defeat, what’s next for Brazil? Michael Safi speaks to Latin America correspondent Tom Phillips – watch on YouTube
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Lula beat far-right Bolsonaro in Brazil – The Latest

articles.author: Jon Henley and Ana Milosavljevic in Belgrade
articles.description:
Non-hierarchical movement is seeking to ‘rebuild society’ in Balkan country after years of authoritarian rule
Serbia’s triumphant but untested Student List movement is preparing to start talks on forming a government capable of reversing 14 years of increasingly authoritarian nationalist rule, after a seismic weekend election win.
Supporters of the movement, which has no experience of government, took to the streets in the west Balkan country on Monday after the strongman former president, Aleksandar Vučić, was defeated in a historic landslide.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Serbia’s Student List preparing for talks on forming government despite no clear leader

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now); Martin Belam, Yohannes Lowe, Adam Fulton and Marina Dunbar (earlier)
articles.description:
Leftist president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated the far-right senator and was elected president of Brazil for a fourth non-consecutive term

Full report: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil’s president over Flávio Bolsonaro

Live second round results

The local electoral court ordered the immediate restoration of 100% of the bus fleet and ordered the arrest of the municipal transport secretary, Pablo Souza, on suspicion of an electoral offence and disobeying court orders. The arrest warrant could not be carried out, however, because he is in Paris on what the city government described as an “official mission”, and is not expected to return to Brazil until Monday.
Late in the afternoon, Flávio Bolsonaro also filed requests for voting to be extended by two hours in cities in the states of São Paulo, Paraná and Santa Catarina, but because of heavy rain that he said had prevented voters from turning out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brazil runoff as it happened: world leaders congratulate Lula on historic election win as Bolsonaro refuses to concede

articles.author: Jakub Krupa (now) and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Hopes raised for a reset in relations with EU and other partners following the defeat of authoritarian president

Serbian leader ousted by student movement in seismic election

Back to Serbia, we are expecting to hear from two groups of election monitors in the coming hours: first, very shortly, from Serbia’s Center for Research, Transparency and Accountability (CRTA), and then a bit later from a group of international observers, including from the OSCE, the ODIHR, and the European parliament.
I will keep an eye on their findings and bring you the key lines.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Serbia wakes up to new reality after student-led movement ousts Vučić – as it hapepned

articles.author: Mark Townsend
articles.description:
Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze
Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
A year after the fall of El Fasher, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Gernot Döllner criticised for in-person announcement of major investment in US days before midterm elections
The head of the luxury carmaker Audi is under fire in Germany for appearing at a rally with Donald Trump just days before the US midterm elections, to announce billions of dollars of investment in battleground state Georgia.
Gernot Döllner joined Trump on stage after the US president gave a speech criticised by the head of an elected body of employees at Audi’s parent company, Volkswagen, as being full of “racism, sexism, transphobia [and] contempt for democracy”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Audi boss under fire in Germany for Trump rally appearance

articles.author: Ramon Antonio Vargas and agencies
articles.description:
Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, denies charges that he fatally strangled Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel on the island of Okinawa
Prosecutors in Japan have filed formal charges against a US marine suspected of murdering and robbing a woman while stationed on the country’s island of Okinawa, according to Japanese media.
Devin Jacob Ballard, a 20-year-old lance corporal assigned to Marine Corps Air Station Futenma in Okinawa, is charged with fatally strangling Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in the city and stealing from her a backpack containing a wallet, the public broadcaster NHK reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japanese prosecutors charge US marine suspected of robbing and killing woman

articles.author: Mark Townsend in Kismayo
articles.description:
Exclusive: Coordinated airstrikes on territory held by al-Shabaab are driving the civilian population to find refuge alongside a river where rising water levels are a threat to safety. Is it a deliberate military strategy?
The water was rising rapidly. It had already reached Cayni Ali’s waist. Her home, five metres from the flooded River Juba in southern Somalia, never stood a chance. There was nowhere to go. Ali’s city of Jilib was under attack. Repeated airstrikes, said the mother of six, were pinning its population beside the rising river.
“The drones come all the time,” said the 27-year-old. “We hear them constantly. They kill animals, civilians. The town is big but destruction is everywhere.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US forces accused of ‘weaponising’ Somalia’s floods by trapping women and children in the path of El Niño

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Khartoum
articles.description:
Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army
Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said.
The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref and one in White Nile state, “resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states”, the official said on condition of anonymity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sudan paramilitary drone strikes cause mass power cuts in eastern states

articles.author: Amy Hawkins in Beijing
articles.description:
Faced with a stagnant jobs market, many are spurning children or pets in favour of ‘raising bricks’
Young adults in China looking for a cheaper, low-maintenance alternative to having children or pets have found an answer: raising bricks.
Bricks may not be as cuddly as cats or as life-affirming as human offspring, but they also cost next to nothing. “No cats, no dating, I started raising a brick,” wrote one brick parent on social media.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Zero-energy companionship’: bizarre hobby takes seed among China’s stressed young adults

articles.author: Julian Borger, Sufian Taha and Quique Kierszenbaum in Hebron
articles.description:
Families forced to flee as Netanyahu tries to prove security credentials after two Israeli soldiers killed days before election
Hebron, the biggest city in the West Bank, had paid little attention to Israel’s looming elections until it found itself suddenly in the midst of them, a proving ground for Benjamin Netanyahu’s security credentials in the run-up to Tuesday’s vote.
A gun attack on an Israeli military checkpoint on Friday in which two soldiers were killed brought immediate televised visits from Netanyahu and his finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, whose ruling coalition is narrowly trailing with two days of campaigning left.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s collective punishment’: nearly 2,000 Palestinians in Hebron displaced as Israeli forces take over homes

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Calculations from the Center for Global Development say spending next year is likely to be £410m less than anticipated
The UK is on course to miss its target of spending 0.3% of national income on international aid by an estimated £400m by the end of next year.
Calculations from the Center for Global Development (CGD) found the UK was on course for a large shortfall in promised official development assistance at the end of 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK poised to miss reduced aid spending target of 0.3% of national income

articles.author: Amy Hawkins in Beijing
articles.description:
The fifth plenum comes against a backdrop of years of purges that have had some analysts wondering if the issue is corruption or a lack of loyalty
When Xi Jinping came to power in 2012, he pledged to stamp out corruption all through the ranks of the Communist party. More than a decade later, the pace of investigations has not slowed. Last year, China’s disciplinary authorities opened investigations into more than 1 million people, including more than 100 officials at or above ministerial or provincial level.
As Chinese Communist party (CCP) officials kick off an important meeting this week, discipline – and party loyalty – is high on the agenda. For those who try to read the tea leaves of elite Chinese politics, concern about the apparent lack of discipline is dominating CCP discussions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Xi Jinping’s corruption crackdown in the spotlight as China prepares for meeting of top leaders

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Exclusive: Forensic analysis of found images continues as Meghan’s father denies possessing child sexual abuse images
All signs point to Thomas Markle Sr being a “possible sex offender of the grossest kind” although a full forensic investigation will give a “definitive picture”, the Philippine interior minister has told the Guardian.
Authorities in the south-east Asian country are analysing digital images allegedly belonging to the estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex that were said to have been found at his former home in Cebu. Meghan’s half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, reported to authorities last week that he had apparently discovered a stash of child sexual abuse images.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Signs suggest Thomas Markle Sr may be ‘sex offender of the grossest kind’, says Philippine minister

articles.author: Oliver Holmes in Bangkok
articles.description:
Kim Aris tells the Guardian chance to speak with detained Nobel laureate was ‘public relations’ move from military leaders
Myanmar’s former democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi appears to be in good physical and mental health but is living in near-complete isolation, her son has said after the first call with his 81-year-old mother in more than five years.
“She still sounds certainly all there mentally, and physically she sounds strong,” Kim Aris said. “I don’t think she has anybody outside of the military or the police around her, so essentially she’s been held in solitary confinement from what I gather.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi ‘sounds strong’ but is isolated, son says

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus

articles.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
articles.description:
Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed
The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.
From next month, 137 cancer drugs in India will be cheaper as the government tries to tackle the tragedy of poorer patients either forgoing treatment, selling land or falling into debt to meet the high cost of some medicines, which are making large profits for hospitals and pharmacists.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’

articles.author: Agence France-Presse in Yangon
articles.description:
Kim Aris says ‘hearing her voice again means more than words can express’ amid loosening of detention restrictions
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi has been allowed to speak to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aung San Suu Kyi’s son speaks to detained former Myanmar leader for first time in five years

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown
An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.
The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday
India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.
Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Chris Hippensteel, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

What are the US midterm elections and why do they matter?


Sign up for Breaking News US email

In a post to social media on Monday, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine was facing dwindling stocks of Patriot interceptor missiles after Pete Hegseth, Trump’s defense secretary, had delayed authorizing new supplies.
“We have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr. Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS,” Zelenskyy wrote. “I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again. Conversations with other countries are also ongoing.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump continues midterm campaign blitz in Mississippi amid outcry over racist, Islamophobic attacks – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
This is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to challenge states with competitive midterm races that could determine control of Congress
The Trump administration on Monday asked Washington state to set aside any ballots received from more than 400 people it alleges are registered to vote without US citizenship, less than two weeks after making a similar demand in California.
The announcement is the latest sign of the administration’s attempts to sow doubts about the election or its outcome in states with races that will help determine control of the US Senate and House.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration asks Washington to set aside hundreds of ballots from suspected noncitizen voters

articles.author: Nick Robins-Early
articles.description:
Newsom accuses Trump of ‘assault on democracy’ as DoJ claims 20,000 registered voters in state are non-citizens
A US federal appeals court rejected the Trump administration’s move to block California from counting the ballots of 20,000 registered voters that the justice department claims are non-citizens.
The court on Monday ruled 2-1 against Donald ⁠Trump’s ​justice department in the dispute, denying the administration’s demand that election officials segregate the thousands of ballots until people on the list could verify their citizenship. The justice department had given the California secretary of state 48-hours to carry out the order, which state election officials refused – leading to the lawsuit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Court blocks bid by Trump DoJ to stop California from counting mail-in ballots

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
President’s comments come ahead of November midterm elections and follow his claims of widespread voter fraud
Donald Trump has announced a $1m reward for reports of voter fraud in past elections and the upcoming midterm elections, with payment contingent on the arrest and conviction of those responsible.
In a Truth Social post on Monday, the president wrote: “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud! Thank you for your attention to this matter.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump dangles $1m reward for reporting voter fraud in past or upcoming elections

articles.author: Sam Levine
articles.description:
Comey, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, accused of leaking information related to US national defense
The justice department charged former FBI director James Comey on Monday with two counts of leaking information related to national defense, the third time the Trump administration has filed criminal charges against one of Donald Trump’s most despised foes.
The charges, filed in federal court in Washington DC, provide few details about what Comey is alleged to have leaked. The government alleges that the former FBI director leaked the information in 2016 and conspired with an unnamed person to give the information to a national news outlet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Justice department charges ex-FBI director James Comey for third time

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Rapper Nicki Minaj joined Donald Trump at a campaign rally in Michigan on 25 October 2026, a final stretch before the 2026 midterm elections, and doubled down her support for the president, saying she would back him again. Trump has recently seemed to concede that he's constitutionally prohibited from serving a third term
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nicki Minaj tells Trump she would support him if he could run for president again – video

articles.author: Jessica Glenza in Escanaba, Michigan
articles.description:
Democrats in the midterms are finally backing Medicare for All as a campaign issue amid a rising tide of US support
Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic US Senate candidate, starts this day on the campaign trail in Escanaba, Michigan, where nearby Wisconsin dairy country spills into dense forests and the sandy shores of Green Bay.
This is the upper peninsula – the “UP” – a rural slash of land north of Michigan’s mitt. Electorally, it’s crimson. Donald Trump won some districts near Escanaba by more than 41%. But at the county fairgrounds, past sheds labeled “Beef” and “Swine”, hundreds of locals on the political left have gathered in the hangar-size 4H Club meeting hall to hear El-Sayed speak.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is universal healthcare finally becoming a vote-winning issue in US elections?

articles.author: Steven Greenhouse
articles.description:
The president’s policies have taken such a toll on farmers that Republicans face trouble in deep-red states
Donald Trump’s policies have been a disaster for the nation’s farmers, so much so that a near electoral miracle may soon happen: Kansas, one of the deepest red, most rural states, may elect its first Democratic senator in nearly a century.
Since Trump won farm country handily in 2024, many rural voters in Kansas, Iowa and elsewhere have soured on him because the price of diesel fuel, a key input for farming, has soared by nearly 70%, because farm bankruptcies have surged and because Trump’s trade wars have significantly reduced agricultural exports.
Steven Greenhouse is a journalist and author, focusing on labor and the workplace, as well as economic and legal issues
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump has been a disaster for rural America | Steven Greenhouse

articles.author: Stephen Starr in Fairborn, Ohio
articles.description:
In a reliably red state, candidates say dissatisfied voters tell them they’re planning to vote Democratic for the first time
Democrat Kim McCarthy is canvassing in a middle-class Ohio neighborhood of four-bedroom, three-bathroom homes. There are $70,000 trucks in the driveways and robot lawnmowers at work.
“This is a neighborhood of two incomes and young families; people working hard,” says McCarthy, who is running against a three-time Republican incumbent for a seat in Ohio’s house of representatives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Discontent with Trump buoys Democrats in Ohio: ‘People are disgusted by the corruption’

articles.author: Jan-Werner Müller
articles.description:
No election outcome ever interprets itself. So how will Democrats interpret these results once they are known?
Whichever metaphor one prefers – landslide, earthquake, wave – it seems increasingly like the Democrats can expect a significant victory in the midterms.
As the joke goes, every gas station display of prices has become an ad for Democrats; what’s more, some of them have managed to connect the relatively abstract issue of corruption to the daily misery of many Americans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: If Democrats win big, will they learn the right lessons from their victory? | Jan-Werner Mueller

articles.author: Rachel Leingang in Arthur, Nebraska
articles.description:
Democratic and independent candidates stump the US midwest and prairie states, hoping to win over Republican strongholds
In this final stretch of the US midterm elections, Democrats and independents could win back communities and towns across America’s rural heartlands through a combination of resurgent “prairie populism”, local despair over the impact of Donald Trump’s agenda and an old-fashioned tenet of shoe-leather politics: showing up everywhere.
When Dan Osborn rolled into one of the most rural counties in Nebraska earlier this month, he started walking into businesses in the tiny main drag of Arthur, ready to meet whomever he could in the town of about 100.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Prairie Populists’ fight to win back rural voters long ceded to Republicans

articles.author: Andrew Gumbel in Lone Pine, California
articles.description:
How a rebuilt, historic California baseball diamond embodies ‘the contradictions in America’s legacy’
When Dan Kwong first dreamed of staging baseball games at the Japanese American concentration camp where his family was held captive during the second world war, he thought of it as an exercise in living history, an eye-catching way to convey the trauma of 120,000 men, women and children who were locked up in the wake of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
Baseball was a passion for Kwong, a 71-year-old performance artist from Los Angeles. He knew that the wartime internees had played the game not just as a distraction from their predicament, but as a quiet expression of their loyalty to the United States. He wanted to stage an event that would cast the game as an act of resistance, and teach new generations about the damage governments do when they strip a whole segment of the population of their constitutional rights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A child of Japanese incarceration’s call to arms: ‘The lessons of Manzanar have never been more urgent’

articles.description:
Barack Obama headlined a rally for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the US Senate, in Detroit on the first day of early voting in Michigan. The former US president told thousands of supporters at Cass technical high school that the 3 November election was an 'inflection point' for American politics

Obama rallies rapturous Michigan crowd for El-Sayed: ‘He’ll finish the job we started’

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Obama throws support behind El-Sayed as early voting begins in Michigan – video

articles.author: Steve Bloomfield
articles.description:
We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise
In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world.
In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield

Donald Trump told rally-goers on Thursday evening that he had 'the right to run again' for president, invoking a claim he has repeatedly made that he may seek a third term despite it being unconstitutional
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump floats unconstitutional third term at campaign rally in Iowa – video

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
Republicans are resorting to childish taunts to defend an uncommonly dishonorable state attorney general
It’s a bit like Lucy with the football. Every few years, Democrats convince themselves that a Texas Senate seat might finally switch from red to blue. On paper, it makes sense. Texas is a large and urbanizing state with an increasingly educated – and increasingly non-white – population.
Other one-time Republican strongholds that have undergone similar demographic shifts have turned purple or even blueish – think Georgia, for example. The border counties along the Rio Grande valley, with their deep poverty and big Latino populations, were long thought to be fertile ground to nurture a kind of anti-Trump populism that could be converted into pro-Democratic sentiment. The state Democratic party is anemic there, but a few talented candidates have emerged.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: A Democratic win in Texas is a long shot – but Ken Paxton’s weakness is obvious | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Shrai Popat, Hazel Tang, John Farrell, Karif Wat
articles.description:
To reclaim control of the Senate, Democrats need to retain all the Senate seats they have and flip four more in the 2026 midterm elections.  Shrai Popat, the Guardian's US politics reporter, explains which are the key races to watch in November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: These key races in the 2026 midterms will decide who controls the US Senate – video explainer

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Tasks from determining asylum seekers’ ages to border surveillance now involve AI, says Open Rights Group 
AI has been embedded across the Home Office in near-total secrecy, reinforcing the so-called hostile environment for immigration, according to research.
Tasks from the detection of potential sham marriages to determining the age of asylum seekers and checking through the contents of phones of new arrivals now involve use of the technology, according to a report by Open Rights Group (ORG).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Digital hostile environment’: AI secretly being embedded across Home Office, report claims

articles.author: Phillip Inman Senior economics writer
articles.description:
British Retail Consortium says ‘dam is starting to break on the huge wave of costs’ being kept from consumers
Shop price inflation has risen to the highest level in two and a half years, according to the British Retail Consortium, which warned that “the dam is starting to break” when it comes to retailers trying to limit price rises for customers.
The lobby group said shop price inflation was 2.1% year on year in October, a sharp rise compared with 1.4% in September, and an indication that retailers were beginning to pass on the rising costs of energy and food ingredients since the Middle East conflict broke out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK shop price inflation ‘highest since 2024’ as retailers struggle to limit price rises

articles.author: Patrick Butler and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Controversial mechanism that hit unpaid carers with huge penalties to be scrapped following Guardian investigation
The controversial rule that led to unpaid carers being punished with penalties amounting to thousands of pounds is to be abolished, the Guardian can reveal.
The chancellor, John Healey, is to announce a new digital taper system for carer’s allowance in Wednesday’s budget, effectively ending what is regarded as one of the UK benefit system’s most feared and unfair administrative practices.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Carers allowed to earn over the weekly limit without losing out as ‘cliff-edge’ abolished in the budget

articles.author: Sinéad Campbell
articles.description:
Group was on visit to meet Palestinian children, farmers and civil leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces
An international delegation including British politicians has been barred from entering the West Bank on a trip to meet Palestinian children, farmers and society leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces during olive harvest season.
The delegation of 23 people, including four elected representatives, was drawn from countries including France, Spain, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Greece, Holland, Ireland and the US. It included the Labour MP Clive Lewis, the Scottish National party MP Lara Bird, the Scottish Greens MSP Kate Nevens and the former Labour MP Sam Tarry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British politicians among international delegates barred from entering West Bank

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Brand, charged with rape and sexual assault, was ‘sleeping with people day and night’, former assistant alleges 
Russell Brand had an “insane sexual appetite” and his bad behaviour was “normalised and dismissed” by those around him, his former personal assistant has told a court.
Helen Berger alleged she had seen Brand treat women badly and that she once had to stop his mother and girlfriend walking in on him having sex with someone in his dressing room.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russell Brand had ‘insane sexual appetite’ and his bad behaviour was normalised, trial told

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
Air Chief Marshal Harv Smyth says technological advances will reduce need for human involvement in warfare
A future Royal Air Force will rely on “autonomy not flesh”, its chief said on Monday as he described plans in which Typhoon fighters are accompanied by four AI-enabled drones capable of patrolling hundreds of miles in the distance.
The technological shift would revolutionise warfare, limit the role of military personnel “towards the outside” and ease the pressure on recruitment, Air Chief Marshal Harv Smyth said in a speech in London.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Autonomy, not flesh’: RAF chief outlines AI drone-powered future

More strong winds forecast after Austen and Boelo kill two people and bring travel disruption and flooding

Tell us: have you been affected by Storm Boelo and Storm Austen

A major clean-up operation was under way on Monday after weekend storms caused havoc, with forecasters warning of more strong winds to come.
Two men were killed by falling trees after two named storms, Austen and Boelo, struck parts of the UK, and there was widespread travel disruption, flooding, power cuts and event cancellations.

articles.title: Major clean-up under way after two storms cause havoc in Britain

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Industrial action by senior doctors to begin on 25 November with only emergency cover provided, BMA says
England’s most senior hospital doctors will strike next month in a dispute over their pay and hours, prompting NHS bosses to warn that patients will suffer “pain, discomfort and inconvenience”.
Consultant doctors, who earn an average of £152,000 a year inclusive of overtime and merit awards, will stage a two-day walkout on 25 and 26 November, as hospitals gear up for the extra pressures winter brings.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS consultants to go on two-day strike in England in November

articles.author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
articles.description:
Clarification comes after PM fuelled speculation about EU-UK relationship in series of interviews at weekend
Downing Street has been forced to clarify Andy Burnham’s stance on whether the UK would return to having freedom of movement with the EU after the prime minister said an “honest discussion” was needed on the issue.
Burnham fuelled speculation about a return to freedom of movement in an interview at the weekend, prompting questions about how close the UK could become to Brussels.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 clarifies Andy Burnham’s stance on freedom of movement

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Terry Barker says nationalisation changes who owns the shares, it does not change the rules, while James Wallace says the powers to intervene already exist. Plus a letter from Philip Clayton
Andy Burnham’s instruction to officials to look at all options for Thames Water and not feel constrained (Burnham urges officials to come up with more radical options for Thames Water, 19 October) is welcome, but the options will fail unless they answer the right question.
Thames Water is not ill-regulated. It is extractively regulated. For 30 years the rules have allowed dividends paid from borrowing, debt loaded on to customers and sewage discharged into rivers as the cheaper alternative to investment. The creditors now asking for a further £2.4bn are not an aberration; they are the system working as designed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The regime change we need for Thames Water | Letters

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Move comes after claims that killer had history of using threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons
Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, has launched a review to examine whether opportunities were missed to prevent the murder of the student Henry Nowak.
It follows claims that there were several warning signs that the perpetrator, Vickrum Digwa, had a history of threatening behaviour and an obsession with weapons.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shabana Mahmood launches review into murder of student Henry Nowak

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
The prime minister previously said that he wanted a debate on how Britain can establish a closer relationship
Speaking at his rough sleeping summit in Downing Street this morning, Andy Burnham expanded on the claim he made on Good Morning Britain about tackling rough sleeping being cheaper than ignoring the problem. (See 11.13am.)
He said:
We’ve also got to be conscious when we speak to the rest of the country, the taxpayers of this country, that actually to leave people sleeping rough has financial consequences. It doesn’t work for anybody and it doesn’t work for the public purse, because if you leave people in a position where they are in and out of A&E, and in and out of a hospital bed, that doesn’t make sense for anybody.
There is a rock-solid business case to do something to end homelessness, to put people on a path to recovery, so that they can contribute once again. And that should be the thinking that we take to this conversation.
Burnham is throwing another £432m at a problem he failed to solve in Greater Manchester. Under Labour, rough sleeping has hit record highs – yet their answer is always more taxpayers’ money and more empty promises.
[John] Healey must use his budget this week to cut taxes for working people, get the ballooning benefits bill under control, and stop pushing up energy prices.
John Healey is expected to confirm on Wednesday that the full state pension will rise by £489 to £13,036 – equivalent to 3.9%.
However, the rise will push about one million people on low incomes who rely on the state pension above the £12,570 personal allowance threshold, meaning they would be dragged into paying income tax.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 plays down UK joining EU single market after Burnham suggests referendum would be needed – as it happened

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
As Andy Burnham hosts a rough sleeper summit, frustration mounts over ‘ridiculous bureaucracy’ and lack of hostel places
Martin Fletcher had been homeless for more than 20 years after being made redundant before he finally got accommodation in Sunderland in 2024.
What was the one thing that finally ended his rough sleeping and sofa surfing? “My mindset, mainly,” the 61-year-old said. “The realisation that I was getting old and I couldn’t live like this for ever. And also help from a charity who didn’t judge, who didn’t bombard me with forms – they made me a cup of tea and built up a picture of what I needed and helped me get back on track.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Local services are vital’: Former rough sleepers on what helped them off the streets

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Application made for group claim seeking compensation for companies for alleged overcharging on customer card payments
Visa and Mastercard are being threatened with a potential £5bn lawsuit for allegedly stifling competition and charging UK businesses excessive fees.
The law firms Harcus Parker and Hausfeld have lodged an application at the Competition Appeal Tribunal in hopes of pursuing a group claim that would compensate companies who, they claim, have been overcharged on customer card payments since October 2020.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Visa and Mastercard threatened with potential £5bn UK lawsuit over fees

articles.author: Mark Townsend
articles.description:
Commanders suspected of sexual violence during the largest and fastest slaughter of civilians in more than 30 years have been subjected to travel ban and asset freeze
Senior Sudanese commanders implicated in a “campaign of rape” have been targeted by the UK on the first anniversary of a mass atrocity that saw tens of thousands of civilians killed over several days.
A year after the fall of El Fasher, the British government said it had sanctioned military leaders from both sides in the country’s ongoing conflict whom it suspected of sexual violence during the siege of the city.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK sanctions Sudanese military leaders implicated in El Fasher ‘campaign of rape’

articles.author: Matthew Weaver
articles.description:
London sites to remain open as Prospect and PCS agree to ‘Acas-facilitated talks’ with museum management
A planned strike at the V&A over half-term has been suspended after an improved offer from its management.
Museum staff who were members of the Prospect and Public and Commercial Services (PCS) unions had voted to strike on Thursday and Friday in a dispute over pay and working conditions including inadequate toilet and hydration breaks. The strike would have closed the V&A’s main galleries in south Kensington, as well as V&A East, V&A Storehouse and Young V&A in east London.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Unions suspend planned V&A strike after improved pay offer

articles.author: Hilary Osborne
articles.description:
Retirees will get a personal allowance aligned with the new state pension, but experts say it could get complicated
Retirees in the UK on low incomes are expected to be given a new personal allowance so that they do not have to hand any of their state pension to HMRC.
The full details are due to be revealed by the chancellor, John Healey, in Wednesday’s budget, but here is what we know so far.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey is expected to shield low-income pensioners from income tax – but how will it work?

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
V2G tech enables drivers to charge automatically when electricity is cheaper and then sell some back to the grid at times of high demand
Electric cars that can be used as “power plants on wheels” could be given government backing as part of plans under consideration to help UK manufacturers.
Ministers are considering giving manufacturers incentives to add “vehicle to grid” (V2G) technology to cars as part of its review of the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK looking to give carmakers incentives to turn EVs into ‘power plants on wheels’

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
R&B singer sentenced to eight months’ imprisonment suspended for 12 months over incident in Mayfair in 2023
The R&B singer Chris Brown has been given a suspended sentence after striking a man twice in the head with a tequila bottle in a central London club.
Brown, 37, admitted affray earlier this year after attacking a former friend with a “heavy” tequila bottle on the dancefloor at the Tape private members’ club in Mayfair in February 2023.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chris Brown given suspended sentence over bottle attack at London club

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Jump fuelled by fears of further Middle East supply disruptions amid reports of US-Israeli plans to strike Iran  
European gas prices have jumped to levels not seen since 2022 as fears continue to grow around the continent’s supply this winter and the conflict in the Middle East.
Wholesale gas prices hit €97 (£81) a megawatt-hour on Monday, as temperatures across Europe fell and traders priced in stronger demand for heating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European gas prices soar to four-year high over winter supply fears

articles.author: Sarah Butler and Gwyn Topham
articles.description:
A stretch of London’s Oxford Street is to be vehicle-free as part of £150m government-backed scheme
Much of Britain’s most famous shopping street will be closed to traffic from Monday as the long-awaited pedestrianisation of London’s Oxford Street begins.
About half of the 1.2 mile street will initially be vehicle-free, after decades of planning and dispute over how to best use the street, an important transport thoroughfare and the home for flagship stores for big shopping chains.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How will pedestrianisation of UK’s most famous shopping street work in practice?

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Monzo says 55% of cardholders’ British Museum payments in first hour of latest ticket release were by people under 35
A 1,000-year-old embroidery may be an unusual candidate for a pop culture moment, but young people are seemingly more willing to shell out for tickets for the Bayeux tapestry than spend money on Hollywood blockbusters.
In the first hour that the second round of tickets to view the tapestry were available last Wednesday, payments from Monzo cardholders to the British Museum reached £14,100 and were 48 times that of a normal Wednesday morning. More than half (55%) of those buyers were aged under 35.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bayeux tapestry becomes pop culture hit as young people more keen to see exhibition than top films

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Josh Halliday; produced by Tom Glasser, Scarlet Pestell, Claudia Efemini and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent

After the prime minister recently intervened to defend Manchester City’s beleaguered ownership, many began to ask: just how deep are the ties between Andy Burnham and the UAE? With North of England editor Josh Halliday. Send your comments and questions to tif.questions@theguardian.com
Why did Andy Burnham recently intervene to defend Manchester City’s beleaguered Abu Dhabi owners, days after they were found guilty of one of the biggest cheating scandals in British sporting history?
Today in Focus presenter and city resident Helen Pidd walks through modern Manchester – where Burnham was mayor for nearly a decade – and charts its transformation wrought by Emirati money.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Abu Dhabi bought Andy Burnham’s Manchester - podcast

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Chancellor was said to be worried about market-sensitive leaks, yet significant policies have been heavily trailed in the media

You be the chancellor: play our budget game to see if you can balance the books

The public has been told repeatedly that John Healey is so concerned about budget leaks that he has set up defence-style “compartmentalisation” to prevent the Treasury’s financial secrets escaping.
The macho military analogies began in mid-August when Healey was said by the Telegraph to be “on a war footing” to stop the drip of information that he believed had beleaguered Rachel Reeves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Has Healey’s military-style budget secrecy really played out so differently to past budgets?

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: People from marginalised groups more likely to be diagnosed via urgent referral or in emergency setting, research finds 
People from minority ethnic backgrounds in England are up to a third less likely to be diagnosed with breast cancer via routine screening, and are more likely to be diagnosed in an emergency setting, analysis has found.
The research, carried out by academics at the University of Surrey and funded by the charity Breast Cancer Now, involved analysis of 86,564 adults diagnosed with the disease between 2009 and 2019, from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink and the Cancer Registration Tumour and Treatment datasets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ethnic minorities in England less likely to get breast cancer diagnosis from routine screening

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Irish and Welsh authors Chris Haughton and Nicola Davies show solidarity after Rooney’s support for Palestine Action
The children’s laureates for Ireland and Wales are donating royalties from their works to Sally Rooney in a show of solidarity after she was forced to stop selling books in the UK because of her support for Palestine Action.
Chris Haughton, Ireland’s children’s literature laureate, said he also wanted to demonstrate the “absurdity” of the bestselling author being unable to receive royalties from her own UK sales because of her public support for the direct action group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two children’s laureates to give royalties to Sally Rooney after her UK sales halted

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Teesside town has come out worst in children’s commissioner’s report, but residents say such rankings are demoralising and counterproductive
“It’s disappointing, it’s just another kicking,” said a youth worker after the town in which they work was labelled as the hardest place in which to be a child in England.
“It suggests our children are living unhappy lives,” said a teacher, who described her pupils as joyful.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Why would I leave?’: Middlesbrough pushes back against ‘hardest place to grow up’ label

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith; the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale
articles.description:
Are we doomscrolling our way into a democratic crisis? That’s what the playwright James Graham fears may be happening, as he suggests that our algorithms have led us into ‘a massive crisis of the new’ and are preventing us from imagining a different future
Watch the full episode with James Graham here.
INK, based on James Graham’s stage play, will be released in UK cinemas on 8 January 2027.
Dear England: about the country’s football team under manager Gareth Southgate.
Sherwood (mentioned in the conversation): set in the village where James grew up in the shadow of the miners’ strike.
Quiz: documenting a notorious scandal on the British gameshow Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Culture is stagnant, so politics is stuck’ – playwright James Graham | Radical Thinking – podcast

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Reality TV show returns to focus on childbirth, diversity and the sharing of stories in a social media age
When One Born Every Minute first aired in 2010, viewers loved its fly-on-the-wall take on life in a maternity unit, from midwives idly chatting about unusual pregnancy cravings to parents squabbling over whether to call their child Zeus.
Almost two decades later, as the show is rebooted for a generation who spend their lives on social media, much has changed. Parents now share far more about their struggles with miscarriages, infertility and mental health; audiences have to be lured away from watching reels on their phones with more rigorous storytelling.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I can’t believe I get to see that’: One Born Every Minute is back for a 12th series

articles.author: Michael Goodier
articles.description:
Sewage samples and crime statistics paint a picture of established users taking more cocaine, more often

Cocaine-linked crimes on the rise in Britain as consumption surges

Pubs, festivals and workplaces: how cocaine has become an everyday habit

From pub toilets and private parties to football terraces and far-right marches, cocaine has become a familiar presence across modern Britain. Deaths linked to the drug have risen to record levels, while its supply supports a multibillion-pound criminal industry.
But who is using the drug, and how has the picture changed? The figures do not necessarily show millions of new users, but highlight an established market in which some people take more cocaine, more often – and face greater harm as they grow older.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ageing users and record deaths – the data behind Britain’s multibillion-pound cocaine habit

articles.author: Press Association
articles.description:
Fresh deluge of wet weather comes after Storm Austen brought strong winds to many regions on Friday
Amber weather warnings have come into force as the worst of Storm Boelo could be set to hit parts of the UK.
Storm Boelo’s winds will peak from Saturday evening, leaving areas in the warning zone, including Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and the far north of England, braced for gusts of 60-70mph and even 80mph in exposed coastal spots, the Met Office said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Boelo: Travel disrupted and events cancelled as UK hit by wind and rain

articles.author: Priya Bharadia
articles.description:
Second named storm will hit northern parts of UK as thousands remain without power after Friday’s Storm Austen
The UK is bracing for a second storm this weekend, as strong winds and heavy rain are expected to disrupt travel and cause further power cuts in the north.
Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Boelo to bring 80mph gusts and heavy rain to parts of UK

articles.author: Tara Conlan
articles.description:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say
The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said.
Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Tim and Geli Harris have spent more than a decade fighting to protect Catfield Fen, a rare wetland in the Norfolk Broads
Polluters and regulators who fail to stop pollution must quake in their boots when they receive a letter from the lawyers for Tim and Geli Harris. The couple, who farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads, have now scored a hat-trick of landmark legal victories to save an internationally important wetland after they won again in the high court this month.
Lady Justice Lieven found that Natural England failed in its statutory duty to protect Catfield Fen from pollution after nitrates and phosphates washed from arable fields into one of the finest examples of calcareous fen in western Europe, home to 2,500 species including rarities such as the fen orchid, crested buckler fern, breeding bittern and swallowtail butterflies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘You need persistence’: the Norfolk couple who took on environmental regulators three times – and won

articles.author: Presented by Aditya Chakrabortty, produced by Frankie Tobi and Luke John Smith; the executive producers are Maz Ebtehaj, Kirsty Major and James Tindale

Are we doomscrolling our way into a democratic crisis? That’s what the playwright James Graham fears may be happening, as he suggests that our algorithms have led us into ‘a massive crisis of the new’ and are preventing us from imagining a different future
